event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Aon’s 2021-02-19 Form 10-K repeatedly links the 2020-onward COVID-19 pandemic to both realised and prospective damage across virtually every dimension of its business model.  The company discloses that results have already been hurt and warns of future ‘materially adverse’ effects, emphasising the pandemic’s breadth (global public-health emergency and economic disruption in every region), depth (credit-market access, litigation exposure, internal-control stress, employee health), and persistence (unknown duration, potential resurgences, new variants).  These statements are recent (within one year of the WHO declaration), specific to Aon, and describe multiple concrete transmission channels—declines in discretionary demand, client insolvency, higher E&O claims, remote-work constraints, liquidity pressure—rather than abstract boiler-plate.  Although the filing notes that full quantification is impossible and mentions some continuity measures, no substantive mitigating controls offset the large, multi-year threat.  Applying the Time Decay Principle (event < 3 years old), evidence can score at the upper end of the scale.  Overall, pandemic risk is assessed as high, with most snippets scoring between 6-8 out of 10.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations have been adversely affected and could be materially adversely affected in the future by the COVID-19 global pandemic.

components.reason: Admits actual negative impact already realised (‘have been adversely affected’).
Projects future ‘materially adverse’ impact, signalling severe forward-looking risk.
Uses strong language (‘materially’) to frame magnitude of risk.
Explicitly attributes risk to the recent COVID-19 pandemic event.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly links COVID-19 to both realised and material future harm, warranting a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 global pandemic has created significant public health concerns and significant volatility, uncertainty, and economic disruption in every region where we operate.

components.reason: Describes widespread (‘every region’) operational and economic disruption.
Emphasises severity with repeated use of ‘significant’.
Explicit reference to COVID-19 as the causal event.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights enterprise-wide disruption and severity; strong but unquantified, scoring 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Such factors include worldwide macroeconomic conditions, including interest rates, employment rates, consumer confidence and spending, gross domestic product, property values, and changes in client behavior, and foreign exchange rates in each of the markets in which we operate; business closures; changes in laws, regulations (including those changes that may provide for extended premium payment terms), and guidance; court decisions and litigation trends; a decline in business and the ability of counterparties to pay for our services on time or at all; an increased number of E&O claims in those areas impacted by the pandemic, as well as an increase in the incidence or severity of E&O claims against us and our market partners; our ability to sell and provide our services, including due to the impact of travel restrictions, lockdowns, quarantines, social distancing, and alternative work arrangements; the health of, and the effect of the pandemic on, our employees; political disruption; potential effects on our internal controls and risk mitigation processes, including those over financial reporting, as a result of changes in working environments for our employees and business partners; resurgences of spread; identification of new, more contagious variants of the virus; resulting “lockdowns,” government restrictions or recommendations; and uncertainties in vaccine manufacturing, accessibility and adoption.

components.reason: Enumerates numerous specific channels of risk (macroeconomics, legal, operational, workforce, variants).
Covers both financial and operational exposures, indicating breadth and depth.
Explicitly tied to the pandemic context.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed list of multi-channel threats shows high severity and specificity; scored 8.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the continuing COVID-19 pandemic may again create significant disruptions in the credit or financial markets, or impact our credit ratings, which could adversely affect our ability to access capital on favorable terms or at all.

components.reason: Flags potential disruption to credit markets and liquidity—critical financial risk.
Highlights possible downgrade to credit ratings affecting capital access.
Links directly to the ongoing pandemic event.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows material financing risk but phrased with conditional ‘may’; moderate-high score 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Finally, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may heighten other risks discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and stock price.

components.reason: States pandemic can amplify multiple existing risk categories.
Covers wide range of potential adverse effects (business, financial, stock price).
Explicit causation by COVID-19.
Conditional language (‘may’) softens certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but less definitive statement, still material; nets to score 5.

evidence_list.snippet: As the situation continues to evolve, and the scale and duration of disruption cannot be predicted, it is not possible to quantify or estimate the full impact that COVID-19 will have on our business.

components.reason: Acknowledges inability to quantify impact—high uncertainty.
Highlights evolving nature and unpredictable duration, elevating risk.
Explicit reference to COVID-19 event.
Unquantifiable risk itself increases perceived severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Emphasises uncontrollable, unpredictable risk; high uncertainty justifies score 7.

evidence_list.snippet: While the ultimate public health and economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic is highly uncertain, we expect that our business operations and results of operations, including our net revenues, earnings, and cash flows, will be adversely impacted, depending on the duration and severity of the downturn, as well as governmental or other regulatory policies and actions that may impact our business or operations.

components.reason: States expectation of adverse impact on multiple financial metrics.
Acknowledges high uncertainty about magnitude and duration.
Direct link to COVID-19 event.
Contingent phrasing (‘depending on’) slightly tempers certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Predicts adverse financial effects but with contingent wording; scores a solid 6.
